name: Khwarezmian
confidence_why: Henning 1956, MacKenzie 1989 and Edel'man 1999 all describe a stem stress that shifts onto the final vowel before suffixes and enclitics, Bogoljubov 1961 is compatible and differs only in reading the tashdid of some enclitic forms as gemination rather than a stress mark, and the one reservation is that every account calls the evidence from the unvocalized Arabic-script texts tentative.

При наращении к слову суффиксов, энклитик или второй части композита удлинялся его конечный гласный после последнего согласного (...). Это изменение также связывают с переносом ударения на данный конечный гласный слова, причем начальный безударный гласный, став еще более удаленным от ударения, мог редуцироваться и утрачиваться
new_statements.translation: Stress fell on the stem; the place of word stress could, presumably, change depending on two factors: 1. A word standing before a pause (at the end of a phrase or in isolation) takes a so-called 'pausal' form with a lengthened vowel before the last consonant (...). This is assumed to be the result of a transfer of stress onto that vowel, cf. st'rk 'star', before pause st'ryk (see also 5.1.2). 2. When suffixes, enclitics or the second member of a compound are added to a word, its final vowel after the last consonant was lengthened (...). This change too is connected with a transfer of stress onto that word-final vowel, whereby an initial unstressed vowel, now still further from the stress, could be reduced and lost [cf. uδir 'belly' ~ δər-βánd 'girth'].
new_statements.citation: Edel'man, D. I. 1999 [2000]. Xorezmijskij jazyk. In: Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki. III. Vostochnoiranskie jazyki, 95-105. Moskva: Indrik.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Reconstructed for an extinct language written mostly without vowels: stress basically on the stem (MacKenzie 1989: nouns paroxytone or initial-stressed, i.e. near the beginning of the word, as in Ossetic; verbal personal endings unstressed, augment/initial syllable of imperfects and subjunctives mostly stressed); stress shifts rightward (a) onto the last stem vowel in pre-pausal (citation/isolation) forms, which is written plene, and (b) onto the word-final vowel immediately preceding an added pronominal suffix/enclitic or second compound member. The only direct evidence is plene 'pausal' spellings and the shadda sign in a few vowelled MSS, which MacKenzie judges 'to some extent contradictory' and 'inconclusive'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: nothing said in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: Edelman hedges the whole account with 'предположительно/предполагается'. MacKenzie 1989 lists counter-examples: 2pl imperatives with stressed ending (hiβrífa, packanífa), 2sg forms in pause with final stress (xurī́na), mkn ~ mkñ variation 'inexplicable', imperfects with and without lengthened (stressed) first vowel in equal numbers; monosyllables with shadda may reflect sentence stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Pausal (pre-pause / isolation, i.e. citation-form) shapes differ systematically from sentence-internal shapes, and the stress account is built on that alternation plus enclisis; so the 'word' here is the word-plus-enclitics group, and citation forms are precisely the pausal forms with the rightward-shifted (pre-final-consonant) stress. All evidence is orthographic (13th-14th c. MSS); no living speakers.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Late (Islamic-period) Khwarezmian/Chorasmian, the East Middle Iranian language of Khwarezm attested in Arabo-Persian script c. 11th-14th c. (Muqaddimat al-adab glosses, Qunyat al-munya law-book sentences) = Glottolog khwa1238, ISO xco. Not the Turkic Khorezm dialect of Uzbek. Old/Middle Chorasmian (Aramaic-script coins, Toprak-kala documents) is too fragmentary for any prosodic statement and is not what the quotes describe.

new_statements.quote: [p. 125, § 2] Положение открытой позиции, очевидно, влекло за собой некоторое сокращение длительности неударного гласного, и это отражалось на письме. В закрытой позиции, т.е. с прибавлением к слову энклитик (местоимений, частиц), конечный гласный слова передавался буквой алиф [...] [p. 128, § 8] фатха, когда ею огласовывался конечный согласный слова, обозначала безударный вариант фонемы ā, встречавшийся на конце слов в открытом слоге. [...] ā, которое, следовательно, теряло долготу в исходе слов, но сохраняло ее в закрытой позиции.
new_statements.translation: [p. 125, § 2] The open position [= word-final before pause] evidently entailed some shortening of the duration of the unstressed vowel, and this was reflected in the writing. In the closed position, i.e. when enclitics (pronouns, particles) are added to the word, the word-final vowel was rendered by the letter alif [...] [p. 128, § 8] fatha, when it vocalized the final consonant of a word, marked the unstressed variant of the phoneme ā that occurred at the end of words in an open syllable. [...] ā, which consequently lost its length in word-final position but kept it in closed position.
new_statements.citation: Bogoljubov, M. N. 1961. O nekotoryx osobennostjax arabo-xorezmijskoj pis'mennosti. Narody Azii i Afriki 1961(4): 182-187.

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with and refines the catalog's Edel'man 1999 statement (stress on the stem; pausal vs. sandhi alternations) and with Henning 1956 held by the project (stress moves forward to the final syllable, which lengthens, when a suffix is added): Bogoljubov independently makes the pausal final -ā unstressed/short and the pre-enclitic final -ā long. It adds no placement rule, so it neither confirms nor contradicts a stem/initial reading. Its reading of tashdid as gemination differs from MacKenzie 1989 / Humbach 1989 / MacKenzie 1991 (held by the project), who take shadda as a probable mark of stress on the preceding vowel.
new_statements.rule_in_words: An orthography article, not a phonology; it states no rule for where word stress falls. What it does say: a word-final -ā/-a standing in 'open position' (word- or phrase-final, before pause) is UNSTRESSED and shortened (written without alif, or with fatha on the last consonant), while the same vowel in 'closed position' (with an enclitic pronoun or particle attached) keeps its length and is written with alif. The introduction (p. 124) notes that the orthographic conventions are the main source of what is known about 'the structure of the word, stress and phrasal phonetics' of Khwarezmian. On p. 127 (§ 5) the tashdid in MS C 2311 (k'mm, k'vv, k'hh) is read as partial notation of a real doubling of the sonant after the conjunction kā, not as a stress mark.
new_statements.exceptions: none on stress; alif in open position is otherwise read as a nasalized -ã (sec. 3, 8, 9)
new_statements.identity_note: All material concerns the same variety: the late (12th-13th c.) Khwarezmian of the Arabic-script sources (Zamakhshari's Muqaddimat al-Adab, the Qunyat al-Munya, MS C 2311 of the IVR RAN). No dialect split is described. Bibliographic note: the copy of Bogoljubov read is the reprint in his collected 'Trudy po iranskomu jazykoznaniju' (pp. 124-131), whose own footnote dates the original NAA publication to 1964 no. 4, pp. 182-187, not 1961 as in the citation; the reprint pagination is the only locator available. The stand-in for work 0 (Abstracta Iranica 39098) abstracts Durkin-Meisterernst 2008 'Khwarezmian in the Islamic period', not the 2009 Windfuhr chapter.

readall_conflicts: No source disagrees about placement, because none of the opened works gives a positional rule. One interpretive disagreement is now on record: Bogoljubov (reprint p. 127, sec. 5) reads the tashdid in MS C 2311 forms such as k'mm, k'vv, k'hh as partial notation of a real gemination of the enclitic's initial sonant after the conjunction kā, whereas MacKenzie 1989, Humbach 1989 and MacKenzie 1991 (already held by the project for this item) take shadda/tashdid as a probable mark of stress on the preceding vowel; since the stress readings of MacKenzie and Edel'man lean on that diacritic, Bogoljubov's alternative weakens, without refuting, the diacritic-based evidence. The two other listed works could not be assessed: the Durkin-Meisterernst open URL is the wrong item (an abstract of his 2008 sociolinguistic paper) and Henning 1936 could not be opened.
